input: scheduled: continue work on the repo (develop, deploy, market, sell, support revenue software)

deviations.why: Explore track: free choice, so I skipped the router's Start-here flagship (ids-model-check) and deepened dxf-nesting's algorithm, whose measured 20% gap to the state of the art was the clearest deep problem on offer.

notes: Idea: let placed parts move again. Seeded overlap-minimisation strip compaction (sparrow-style) on dxf-nesting's conservative grid (compact.mjs). Pre-registered on the ESICUP split: on the held-out 13, search 100 + squeeze went 0.8359 -> 0.8526 (bar +0.01), greedy + squeeze 0.8069 -> 0.8358, none worse, all 46 nests pass verify. The worked example takes 7.5 s against the 5 s bar, so it ships opt-in (page select, CLI --compact). A tie-break on an early-exit partial sum hid every gain until fixed. Next: weights per pair of parts (the 161-part gardeyn6 separation diverges). Verification: node --test dxf-nesting 47 pass; run_workflow_locally --for-changes 10/10 selected workflows passed (uses: steps, cross-review and deploy jobs not run locally); post checks pass.
